subject: Architecture
title: Brutalism: Raw Concrete as Philosophy
description: A short lesson to help you apply Brutalism: Raw Concrete as Philosophy.

hook.text: Brutalism showed the raw concrete structure with nothing hidden — honesty as an aesthetic choice.

buildup.text: Post-war Britain needed housing fast. Concrete was cheap, strong, and could be poured into any shape.

discovery.text: The Barbican in London is a Brutalist village — flats, a concert hall, and a lake inside a concrete fortress.

twist.text: Governments used Brutalism for social housing, then neglected the buildings until they became slums.

climax.text: A new generation now campaigns to save Brutalist buildings, calling them bold and authentic.

punchline.text: They built honestly. The neglect was the real crime.

quiz.question: Why was concrete the material of choice for Brutalist architects?
options: It was the most beautiful material available
It was cheap, strong, and could be shaped freely
It was the only material approved by building codes

details.summary: Brutalism used raw, unfinished concrete (béton brut) to create bold, sculptural buildings that expressed structural honesty. Popular from the 1950s through the 1970s, it produced powerful civic buildings worldwide but also became associated with urban decay and social housing failures.
details.whyItMatters: Brutalism forces you to confront architecture without cosmetic comfort. Its honest exposure of materials and structure represents an ethical stance — that buildings should show what they are rather than pretend to be something else.
takeaways: Brutalism used raw, exposed concrete as its primary material
Popular from the 1950s to 1970s for civic and housing projects
It expressed structural honesty but attracted lasting controversy

faq.question: Why is Brutalism so controversial?
faq.answer: Its raw concrete weathers poorly, staining and cracking in ways that look neglected. Many Brutalist social housing projects became symbols of poverty and institutional failure. Yet architecture enthusiasts admire the style's sculptural power and uncompromising honesty.

faq.question: Is Brutalism making a comeback?
faq.answer: Yes. Instagram and architectural photography have revived appreciation for Brutalism's bold forms. Many threatened Brutalist buildings have been listed for preservation. New concrete buildings increasingly reference Brutalist aesthetics, though with improved weathering technology.
